canonical_question: Is the '0.5 mV/s' scanning rate for polarization fast enough to avoid steady-state errors in a system with high thermal conductivity like W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V?

question_variants.question: Is the '0.5 mV/s' scanning rate for polarization fast enough to avoid steady-state errors in a system with high thermal conductivity like W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states the scanning rate was 0.5 mV/s but does not evaluate if this rate is fast or slow enough to avoid steady-state errors in high thermal conductivity systems.

answers.answer: The scanning rate for the potentiodynamic polarization analysis was 0.5 mV/s. The provided text does not discuss the thermal conductivity of the W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V system in relation to this rate, nor does it evaluate the risk of steady-state errors.
answers.mechanism: None provided regarding thermal conductivity effects on polarization.
answers.boundary_limitation: No data linking scan rate to thermal conductivity or steady-state error.
evidence_spans: The printing parameters of these trials were varied as follows: laser power 160–244 W, spot size 80 µm, scanning speed 300–700 mm/s, hatch spacing 0.10–0.12 mm, building layer thickness 0.3 mm, energy density 38.1–162.7 [J/mm 3 ] and final obtained densities 38–95 [%], as shown in Table 3 .
